Feature.Description:
SiLA2 feature for Opentrons Flex gantry and pipette motion.
Provides homing, absolute and relative mount moves, position queries, primitive aspirate/dispense, emergency stop, and deck/status lights via the Opentrons ``OT3API``.

Command.Description: Draw liquid into the attached tip.

Parameter.Description: Flow-rate multiplier on the pipette's configured aspirate rate.

Command.Description: Blow out any residual liquid from the attached tip.
Expel liquid from the attached tip.

Parameter.Description: Flow-rate multiplier on the pipette's configured dispense rate.
Extra plunger push-out volume in µL (0 = pipette default).

Command.Description:
Expel liquid from the attached tip and stop the plunger at its bottom position.
Unlike Dispense, no push-out follows even when the tip is emptied, so the pipette stays ready to aspirate in place. Use it for the dispense half of a mix cycle.

Parameter.Description: Flow-rate multiplier on the pipette's configured dispense rate.

Command.Description: Immediately halt all motion. A re-home is required before resuming.

Response.Description: A status message confirming the stop.

Command.Description: Return the current deck position of ``mount`` in mm.
Home every axis. Required after an emergency stop before further motion.
Home only the axes belonging to one mount.

Parameter.Description: Mount to home (its Z and plunger/jaw axes).

Command.Description: Move a mount relative to its current position.

Parameter.Description: Movement speed in mm/s (0 = hardware default).

Response.Description: The mount position after the move.

Command.Description: Move a mount to an absolute deck position.

Parameter.Description: Movement speed in mm/s (0 = hardware default).

Response.Description: The mount position after the move.

Command.Description: Move the plunger to its bottom position, ready to aspirate.
Resume motion execution after a pause.
Set the status-bar (button) and deck (rails) lights.

Response.Description: The light state after the change.

Property.Description: Whether the connector is driving the OT3 simulator rather than real hardware.
Return the current status-bar and deck light state.

Return the robot safety/error state (E-stop, door) independent of any move.
A movement command can return successfully while the robot has silently entered a hardware error state. Read this property after each movement to confirm the move genuinely succeeded: ``is_error_state`` is True when the robot is in an error state that requires operator intervention.

DefinedExecutionError.Description:
Protocol Engine currently owns the Flex for a prepared or active run.
Read status through the connector as usual, but do not issue an independent SiLA hardware command. Stop the Protocol Engine run, or add the operation at an explicit UNITELABS mutation checkpoint through the controlled run-mutation HTTP endpoint, then retry.

The robot's position is unknown, so the move was refused.
Home the robot (or the affected mount) before requesting a move. If a halt interrupted gripper motion, fully home the robot and then run HomeJaw before resuming other hardware actuation.

The shared Flex hardware stayed busy longer than the configured lock timeout.
Another SiLA client, an HTTP/Protocol Engine operation, or a long-running module action currently holds the hardware. Wait for that operation to finish (watch the RobotStatusProvider Status property) and retry, or raise lock_timeout_s in the connector configuration.

The operation was aborted because an emergency stop or halt was issued while it ran.
The robot position is no longer trusted. Clear the cause of the halt, fully re-home the robot, follow the RecoveryGuidance reported by RobotStatusProvider, and then re-issue the operation.

The connector refused the operation because an earlier failure left the robot recovery-gated.
The error message lists the ordered recovery actions (for example a full re-home, TipController.ReconcileTipState, or GripperController.HomeJaw). The same guidance is available at any time from the RobotStatusProvider Status property.

The Flex hardware reported an error that has no more specific defined error.
The message preserves the Opentrons error code, name, and detail so the cause can be diagnosed or reported to vendor support. Inspect the robot, resolve the reported condition, re-home, and retry.

The requested move would take the mount outside the deck working volume.
Check the target coordinates against the Flex deck envelope and retry.

A stall or collision was detected during the move; motion was halted.
Clear any obstruction, then re-home before continuing. The underlying hardware message is preserved to aid diagnosis.

The move was accepted but the robot has silently entered a hardware error state.
A movement command can return without raising while the machine has already entered an error state (for example the E-stop became engaged mid-move). This error surfaces that hidden condition so callers never treat such a move as successful. Clear the fault (release the E-stop), then re-home before continuing. The underlying hardware state is preserved to aid diagnosis.

Direct gripper actuation is disabled while the durable labware plan registry is active.
Use LabwareMovementController for allowlisted moves. To perform maintenance, stop the connector and explicitly disable the local labware movement configuration.

No pipette is attached to the requested mount.
Attach a Flex pipette, re-scan instruments, and retry the tip operation.

The requested drop was refused because no tip is attached.
Confirm the physical tip state and perform a verified pickup before retrying the drop operation.

DefinedExecutionError.DisplayName: Liquid Volume Out Of Range Error
DefinedExecutionError.Description:
The requested liquid volume is outside the attached pipette's current operating range.
Check the attached pipette model, tip capacity, and liquid already held in the tip. Use a volume within the limits reported by PipetteController and retry.

The pipette failed while preparing, aspirating, dispensing, or blowing out liquid.
Inspect the tip and liquid path, clear any obstruction or overpressure condition, reconcile the physical liquid state, and re-home before retrying. The underlying Opentrons error message is preserved for diagnosis.
